newsitem.title: ITALY: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday March 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Italy - Friday March 14.

text.p: The following are some of the top headlines in leading Italian newspapers.

* Albania's government called for foreign military intervention to halt spreading disorder. Two children of Sali Berisha, the president of the troubled Balkan country, fled to Italy with another dozen Albanians. Some other 40 managed to rush aboard another vessel headed for the Italian southern port of Brindisi (all).

* Italy's centre-left government held a meeting of coalition parties to discuss the Labour Minister's proposals to boost employment. Some new 100,000 jobs will be created in the poorer south with an average 800,000 lire a month salary and around 10 trillion lire funds for "depressed areas" will be unblocked (all).

* Giorgio Fossa, the chairman of Italian industrialists association Confindustria, harshly criticised the new measures saying that the government did not take into account the industrialists need for labour flexibility.(all)

* Deputy Prime Minister Walter Veltroni said coalition difficulties were resolved at the meeting: "The situation has been unblocked, there is political solidarity and this coalitions confirms it intends to last for the entire legislature". (all).
* Hard-left Communist Refoundation party leader Fausto Bertinotti said that during the meeting jobs question had been resolved (all).

* Prime Minister Romano Prodi told chairmen of the upper and lower houses of parliament Nicola Mancino and Luciano Violante that the government will restrain appliance of the new decree law to "emergency situation" (all).
* During a testimony to the Senate finance committee, Finance Minister Vincenzo Visco announced a new regional tax will be introduced (all).

* Insurance group Generali said it had set its $308 million tender offer for shares in Israel's Leumi Insurance Holding for next week. The Italian group added that the final offer price, whose total value is 1.04 billion shekels, would be adjusted for inflation after publication of February's consumers price index (all).

* The swap ratio for Italian state telecoms holding company STET and telecoms operator Telecom Italia is expected to be between 1.82 and 1.95 at their forthcoming merger. The actual ratio is due to be settled at board meetings of the two groups which will take place today. Opposition leader Silvio Berlusconi praised the forthcoming merger calling it a "cautious operation" (all).
* Italian cable laying company Sirti, controlled by state telecoms holding STET, said its consolidated profit fell to 157.7 billion lire in 1996 against 214 billion lire in 1995 (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Newly-formed Gruppo Industriale Marzotto (GIM) said it would welcome foreign partners provided they approved its market policy (Il Sole 24 Ore).
* Italy's largest commercial bank Istituto San Paolo di Torino said it had no comment to make of speculation its planned public sale offer would get underway on May 16 (Il Sole 24 Ore).
Reuters has not verified these stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
